name: Inverse Littlewood-Offord theory (Tao-Vu, Nguyen-Vu, Rudelson-Vershynin, Kwan-Sauermann, Fox-Kwan-Sauermann)
description: Forward Littlewood-Offord (Erdos 1945, Sarkozy-Szemeredi, Halasz) bounds the maximum probability p = max_y P[sum eps_i a_i = y] for random signs/bits. Inverse theory asks what A must look like if p is large: Tao-Vu (2009) showed p >= n^{-O(1)} forces all but few elements of A into a generalized arithmetic progression (GAP) of rank O(1) and size n^{O(1)}; Nguyen-Vu gave the optimal version (essentially p >= n^{-C} implies all but O(1) elements lie in a GAP of rank O(1) and size O(p^{-1} n^{-1/2})); Rudelson-Vershynin phrase it via the least common denominator (LCD) of the coefficient vector; Kwan-Sauermann and Fox-Kwan-Sauermann extend anti-concentration/inverse results to quadratic and combinatorial settings. In the repo's language, a large bin (many subsets with equal sum) forces GAP or dissociated-with-large-sets structure.
authors_year_venue: [uncertain] T. Tao and V. Vu, 'Inverse Littlewood-Offord theorems and the condition number of random discrete matrices', Annals of Math 169 (2009) 595-632; H. Nguyen and V. Vu, 'Optimal inverse Littlewood-Offord theorems', Adv. Math. 226 (2011); M. Rudelson and R. Vershynin, 'The Littlewood-Offord problem and invertibility of random matrices', Adv. Math. 218 (2008); M. Kwan and L. Sauermann, 'An algebraic inverse theorem for the quadratic Littlewood-Offord problem, and an application to Ramsey graphs', Discrete Analysis (2020); J. Fox, M. Kwan, L. Sauermann, 'Combinatorial anti-concentration inequalities, with applications', Math. Proc. Cambridge Philos. Soc. (2021). Also Carpenter-Defant-Kravitz arXiv:2605.05498 (relationship stated in its introduction).
status_and_verification: [uncertain] Peer-reviewed journals (as recalled). NOT checked against the primary texts. The only primary-text check: Carpenter-Defant-Kravitz (arXiv 2605.05498 intro, read) states that [TV09, Thm 2.5 and Cor 2.7] give: if max_y P[S=y] >= n^{-O(1)} then almost all of A lies in a GAP of rank O(1) and size n^{O(1)}. Everything else (Nguyen-Vu optimal form, RV LCD thresholds, KS/FKS statements) is recall and the exact constants are unverified.
key_theorem_or_bound: [uncertain] Verified second-hand (CDK intro citing TV09 Thm 2.5/Cor 2.7): P[S=y] >= n^{-O(1)} implies all but O(1) (almost all) elements of A lie in a GAP of rank O(1), size n^{O(1)}. Recalled, unverified: Erdos-Littlewood-Offord sup P <= C(n,floor(n/2))/2^n for nonzero a_i; Sarkozy-Szemeredi sup P = O(n^{-3/2}) for distinct a_i; Nguyen-Vu optimal form: P >= n^{-C} implies all but O(1) of the a_i lie in a symmetric GAP of rank r=O(1) and volume O(P^{-1} n^{-r/2}) (exponent form to be checked); RV: P <= C/(sqrt n) ... + exp(-c n) controlled by 1/LCD-type quantities.
regime_exponents: [uncertain] Polynomial-concentration regime: P >= n^{-O(1)}. The repo's large-bin regime is exponential (N_t or bin size about 2^{epsilon n}, i.e. P about 2^{-(1-epsilon)n}); classical inverse LO says nothing there, although Fourier/Halasz-type arguments extend to P >= 2^{-cn} with rank growing. No statements about D* thresholds (0.311n), 0.5n, 0.661n.
proof_type_and_tools: [uncertain] Fourier/analytic (Esseen, Halasz inequality, large spectrum of the characteristic function, Bohr sets) combined with the Freiman-Bilu structure theorem and geometry of numbers (Tao-Vu); LCD and Esseen's concentration inequality (RV); Nguyen-Vu use a sharper counting argument with arithmetic structure. Named lemmas: Halasz-type L^p estimates, Freiman-Bilu, Chang-type spectrum control, covering lemmas.
quantitative_loss: [uncertain] Rank O(1) and size n^{O(1)} with huge implicit constants in TV09 (exponential in the exponent C); Nguyen-Vu are near-optimal in the polynomial regime. For P = 2^{-Omega(n)} the GAP rank grows linearly and the conclusion becomes vacuous (a rank-n GAP of size 2^n contains everything), so the bound does not survive exponential energy.
worst_case_vs_average_case: Worst case over the coefficient vector A (adversarial a_i), probabilistic over the signs/bits; conclusion is structural for the given A. Transfer to the worst-case algorithmic question needs the large bin to be the specific bin containing a solution.
coefficient_set: [uncertain] Original statements for symmetric {-1,1} signs; the {0,1} version follows by translation (eps in {0,1} is (1+eta)/2, shifting by half the total) at a loss of a factor-2 rescaling of A. Also multiset (repeated a_i) versions, which is where the GAP structure appears.
subset_size_regime: [uncertain] All subsets drawn uniformly (Bernoulli(1/2) bits), which concentrates on size n/2 +- sqrt(n); slice versions (fixed size Theta(n)) require extra work (uniform on a layer, Kwan-Sauermann-type permutation/slice results are not verified by me).
relevance_to_Nc: [uncertain] A large bin means many subsets with equal sum, equivalently many equal-sum pairs; bin of size B = 2^n P gives about B^2/(2^n)... collision count at least B^2 / (number of bins) after Cauchy-Schwarz, hence N_c large iff the maximum/typical bin is large. Inverse LO structure (GAP of rank r) then expresses N_c in terms of the GAP geometry. This is the 'large-bin' branch of the repo's dichotomy (AKKN: concentration gives structure; absence of concentration gives a faster algorithm).
relevance_to_Dstar: [uncertain] If D* is small, then T(S1,S2) is a small sumset of two (n/8)-slice sums, which makes the distribution of the half-sums highly concentrated (a bin of size at least C(n/4,n/8)^2/D*). Inverse LO would then place most of the support S inside a low-rank GAP. This could be the engine to forbid D* <= 2^{0.311n} for non-GAP hard instances, but only if the inverse theorem can be run at exponential concentration with rank growing slowly, which classical results do not give.
applicability_gap: [uncertain] (i) Concentration threshold n^{-O(1)} versus 2^{-Theta(n)}; (ii) rank O(1) versus rank growing with n; (iii) uniform over all subsets versus Theta(n)-slices (D* uses slice sums of size n/8); (iv) constants are not explicit enough to be applied at n<=40; (v) the structural conclusion 'almost all of A in a GAP' discards O(1)-many outliers, which a worst-case algorithm may not ignore.
counterexample_or_hard_instance_family: [uncertain] Rank-d GAPs with random generators (concentration 2^{-Theta(n)} yet dissociated-like once d is about n/log n); AP {1..n} (maximal concentration); box supports in [0,L)^d (repo); dissociated sets (no concentration, P about 2^{-n}); Sidon-like sets with P = n^{-3/2}-type behaviour (distinct-element extremals).
dependency_chain: [uncertain] Natural first step in a branch-or-bin argument: large bin implies GAP via inverse LO (this item) or Fourier large spectrum (fourier_large_spectrum_bohr) implies, via Freiman/Bilu/BSG, a low-rank structure that is then detected by lattice_relation_detection; absence of bin concentration is where dissociated_sidon_structure and distinct_subset_sums_extremal apply.
constructiveness: [uncertain] Mostly non-constructive; the Rudelson-Vershynin LCD framework is computable (LCD can be approximated by lattice methods), and Chen-Mao-Zhang constructive APs apply in the dense regime only.
lean_formalizable: [uncertain] Unlikely for the full theorems (Freiman-Bilu, Halasz, geometry of numbers). The forward Erdos-Littlewood-Offord bound (Sperner-based) is formalizable without mathlib.
computational_check: [uncertain] Not tested numerically in any source I read. In the repo, at n<=40 the maximum bin and N_c can be computed exactly via meet-in-the-middle histograms of subset sums for random and structured families, and compared with a rank-r GAP fit; no scripts verified by me.
next_experiment: [uncertain] For the repo's hard-instance families at n=24 and 32, compute the full histogram of subset sums, the max bin B, and the minimal-rank GAP (via the relation lattice) covering 90 percent of the support; plot log2(B)/n against rank/n to see whether exponential concentration forces rank growth linear in n.
open_issues: [uncertain] Whether an inverse LO theorem holds with exponential concentration and slowly growing rank is exactly the missing piece; no source verified; all names/years/venues for Nguyen-Vu, RV, Kwan-Sauermann, Fox-Kwan-Sauermann come from recall.
